title: Criminal Law I
topics: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Conversion.
o: the dishonest taking of another's property with intent permanently to deprive
a killing that the law permits, as in the execution of a lawful death sentence
serious bodily injury that endangers life or causes lasting damage
dealing with another's property as though one were its owner
items.s: Conversion: dealing with another's property as though one were its owner. The other options describe Grievous harm, Justifiable homicide, Theft.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Retribution?
o: the aim of punishment that seeks to give a deserved response to wrongdoing
an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means
the requirement that the conduct be a substantial and operating factor in bringing the result about
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
items.s: Retribution: the aim of punishment that seeks to give a deserved response to wrongdoing. The other options describe Legal causation, Conspiracy, Kidnapping.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Excusable homicide.
o: the aim of punishment that seeks to give a deserved response to wrongdoing
the rule that an accused takes the victim as found, even with a hidden weakness
the dishonest taking of another's property with intent permanently to deprive
a killing for which the actor is not blamed, as in a pure accident without fault
items.s: Excusable homicide: a killing for which the actor is not blamed, as in a pure accident without fault. The other options describe Thin skull principle, Retribution, Theft.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Consent?
o: a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless
the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
a person who assists or encourages beforehand without being present at the act
the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him
items.s: Consent: the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him. The other options describe Accessory before the fact, Mistake of fact, Abduction.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence”?
o: Insanity
Infancy
Duress
Intoxication
items.s: Infancy is the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Alibi.
o: the use of no more force than is needed to repel an immediate unlawful attack
the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place
the dishonest taking of another's property with intent permanently to deprive
the aim or purpose of an actor to bring about a result
items.s: Alibi: the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place. The other options describe Intention, Private defence, Theft.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Civil wrong?
o: an infringement of a private interest that the injured person redresses by action
any offence that the law does not class as a felony and that carries a lighter penalty
the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him
pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice
items.s: Civil wrong: an infringement of a private interest that the injured person redresses by action. The other options describe Misdemeanour, Consent, Duress.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Conspiracy?
o: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent
the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer
an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means
setting fire to a building or other property unlawfully
items.s: Conspiracy: an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means. The other options describe Reformation, Regulatory offence, Arson.

items.q: Preparation may be defined as
o: awareness that a certain fact exists
the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place
a taking of property by a person carrying a dangerous weapon at the time
putting the means in place for a crime before any step that comes near completing it
items.s: Preparation: putting the means in place for a crime before any step that comes near completing it. The other options describe Knowledge, Alibi, Armed robbery.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Recklessness.
o: a mental disorder so severe that the accused did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong
awareness of a risk that a result will follow, yet going ahead anyway
a failure to act where the law imposes a duty to act
responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element
items.s: Recklessness: awareness of a risk that a result will follow, yet going ahead anyway. The other options describe Omission, Insanity, Strict liability.

items.q: The statement “awareness that a certain fact exists” describes which of the following?
o: Negligence
Mens rea
Knowledge
Intention
items.s: Knowledge is awareness that a certain fact exists.

items.q: Capital offence may be defined as
o: awareness of a risk that a result will follow, yet going ahead anyway
a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless
an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means
a crime for which the law prescribes the death penalty
items.s: Capital offence: a crime for which the law prescribes the death penalty. The other options describe Recklessness, Involuntary manslaughter, Conspiracy.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Reformation?
o: the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer
putting the means in place for a crime before any step that comes near completing it
a crime for which the law prescribes the death penalty
items.s: Reformation: the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer. The other options describe Capital offence, Abduction, Preparation.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Which term is described by “taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen”?
o: Robbery
Conversion
Receiving
Theft
items.s: Receiving is taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen.

items.q: Regulatory offence may be defined as
o: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent
conduct that would make a reasonable person lose self-control and act in the heat of the moment
responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element
carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree
items.s: Regulatory offence: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent. The other options describe Strict liability, Provocation, Defilement.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Private defence?
o: an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means
the duty of a party to establish a fact in issue to the satisfaction of the court
the use of no more force than is needed to repel an immediate unlawful attack
the aim of punishment that seeks to give a deserved response to wrongdoing
items.s: Private defence: the use of no more force than is needed to repel an immediate unlawful attack. The other options describe Retribution, Conspiracy, Burden of proof.

items.q: Indictable offence may be defined as
o: the aim or purpose of an actor to bring about a result
a charge tried by a magistrate without any formal indictment
a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial
dealing with another's property as though one were its owner
items.s: Indictable offence: a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial. The other options describe Intention, Conversion, Summary offence.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Deterrence?
o: the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place
the prohibited conduct or consequence, with any required circumstances, that makes up the physical side of an offence
items.s: Deterrence: the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct. The other options describe Beyond reasonable doubt, Actus reus, Alibi.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Which of the following best describes Misdemeanour?
o: any offence that the law does not class as a felony and that carries a lighter penalty
taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen
the prohibited conduct or consequence, with any required circumstances, that makes up the physical side of an offence
a person who assists or encourages beforehand without being present at the act
items.s: Misdemeanour: any offence that the law does not class as a felony and that carries a lighter penalty. The other options describe Actus reus, Receiving, Accessory before the fact.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Infancy?
o: a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial
the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
a mental disorder so severe that the accused did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong
items.s: Infancy: the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence. The other options describe Insanity, Indictable offence, Beyond reasonable doubt.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Infancy.
o: the urging or encouragement of another to commit a crime
any act or omission for which the law imposes a penalty
an outward deed showing that a criminal purpose has moved beyond mere thought
the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence
items.s: Infancy: the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence. The other options describe Overt act, Incitement, Offence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the failure to take the care that a reasonable person would take in the circumstances”?
o: Transferred malice
Mens rea
Knowledge
Negligence
items.s: Negligence is the failure to take the care that a reasonable person would take in the circumstances.

items.q: Which term is described by “a person who advises or instructs another beforehand to carry out the crime”?
o: Accessory before the fact
Counsellor
Accessory after the fact
Principal offender
items.s: Counsellor is a person who advises or instructs another beforehand to carry out the crime.

items.q: Duress may be defined as
o: the care shown by taking all reasonable steps to prevent the prohibited result
conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts
pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice
the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct
items.s: Duress: pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice. The other options describe Deterrence, Crime, Due diligence.

items.q: The statement “an offence committed when a motorist's poor control of a vehicle results in a fatality” describes which of the following?
o: Involuntary manslaughter
Manslaughter
Murder
Causing death by dangerous driving
items.s: Causing death by dangerous driving is an offence committed when a motorist's poor control of a vehicle results in a fatality.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rape?
o: the reason that drives a person to act, which differs from the purpose to break the law
unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
the test asking whether the result would have happened without the conduct of the accused
items.s: Rape: unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement. The other options describe Factual causation, Kidnapping, Motive.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Offence?
o: any act or omission for which the law imposes a penalty
the rule that a guilty state of mind aimed at one person carries over to the person actually hurt
an agreement of two or more persons to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means
the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer
items.s: Offence: any act or omission for which the law imposes a penalty. The other options describe Conspiracy, Transferred malice, Reformation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Involuntary manslaughter?
o: a person who assists or encourages beforehand without being present at the act
pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice
a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless
the taking of property by force or threat of force at or immediately before the taking
items.s: Involuntary manslaughter: a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless. The other options describe Robbery, Accessory before the fact, Duress.

items.q: The statement “pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice” describes which of the following?
o: Duress
Mistake of fact
Private defence
Alibi
items.s: Duress is pressure of threats that overbears the will so that the accused has no real choice.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Legal causation.
o: responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element
the duty of a party to establish a fact in issue to the satisfaction of the court
the actual application of unlawful force to the body of another
the requirement that the conduct be a substantial and operating factor in bringing the result about
items.s: Legal causation: the requirement that the conduct be a substantial and operating factor in bringing the result about. The other options describe Strict liability, Burden of proof, Battery.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Defilement?
o: the duty of a party to establish a fact in issue to the satisfaction of the court
the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree
the state of being under the influence of drink or drugs, which may negate a required state of mind
items.s: Defilement: carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree. The other options describe Burden of proof, Intoxication, Abduction.

items.q: The statement “the rule that an accused takes the victim as found, even with a hidden weakness” describes which of the following?
o: Factual causation
Omission
Thin skull principle
Actus reus
items.s: Thin skull principle is the rule that an accused takes the victim as found, even with a hidden weakness.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Simple offence?
o: a minor infraction tried in a lower court and punished by a small fine or short detention
conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts
unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
items.s: Simple offence: a minor infraction tried in a lower court and punished by a small fine or short detention. The other options describe Rape, Crime, Beyond reasonable doubt.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Beyond reasonable doubt.
o: a person who helps the wrongdoer to escape detection once the act is complete
the aim of punishment that seeks to give a deserved response to wrongdoing
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
a step taken with the purpose of committing a crime that does not reach completion
items.s: Beyond reasonable doubt: the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction. The other options describe Retribution, Accessory after the fact, Attempt.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Mistake of fact.
o: a killing that the law permits, as in the execution of a lawful death sentence
the rule that a child below the age of seven cannot be guilty of any offence
a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless
a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless
items.s: Mistake of fact: a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless. The other options describe Infancy, Justifiable homicide, Involuntary manslaughter.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Concurrence.
o: unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement
the requirement that the prohibited act and the guilty state of mind occur together
the rule that an accused takes the victim as found, even with a hidden weakness
the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
items.s: Concurrence: the requirement that the prohibited act and the guilty state of mind occur together. The other options describe Thin skull principle, Housebreaking, Rape.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Novus actus interveniens?
o: a new intervening event that breaks the chain between the conduct and the result
conduct that would make a reasonable person lose self-control and act in the heat of the moment
awareness of a risk that a result will follow, yet going ahead anyway
carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree
items.s: Novus actus interveniens: a new intervening event that breaks the chain between the conduct and the result. The other options describe Defilement, Recklessness, Provocation.

items.q: Beyond reasonable doubt may be defined as
o: putting the means in place for a crime before any step that comes near completing it
dealing with another's property as though one were its owner
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
items.s: Beyond reasonable doubt: the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction. The other options describe Conversion, Kidnapping, Preparation.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Impossibility.
o: the situation where the intended crime cannot be committed, which may still ground liability for the step taken
the person whose own act fulfils the definition of the crime
the prohibited conduct or consequence, with any required circumstances, that makes up the physical side of an offence
the link that must be shown between the conduct of the accused and the prohibited result
items.s: Impossibility: the situation where the intended crime cannot be committed, which may still ground liability for the step taken. The other options describe Principal offender, Causation, Actus reus.

items.q: The statement “an outward deed showing that a criminal purpose has moved beyond mere thought” describes which of the following?
o: Conspiracy
Attempt
Abandonment
Overt act
items.s: Overt act is an outward deed showing that a criminal purpose has moved beyond mere thought.

items.q: Which term is described by “the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place”?
o: Automatism
Intoxication
Alibi
Duress
items.s: Alibi is the claim that the accused was elsewhere when the act complained of took place.

items.q: Which term is described by “an act that puts another in fear of immediate unlawful force”?
o: Abduction
Rape
Assault
Battery
items.s: Assault is an act that puts another in fear of immediate unlawful force.

items.q: Consent may be defined as
o: responsibility of one person for the act of another, arising from their relationship
a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless
taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen
the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him
items.s: Consent: the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him. The other options describe Mistake of fact, Receiving, Vicarious liability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Kidnapping.
o: a crime for which the law prescribes the death penalty
an offence that the law classes as grave and punishes by death or three years imprisonment and above
the link that must be shown between the conduct of the accused and the prohibited result
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
items.s: Kidnapping: the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority. The other options describe Causation, Felony, Capital offence.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Abettor?
o: a person who incites or encourages the doer at the moment the act takes place
the aim or purpose of an actor to bring about a result
securing property or credit through a dishonest representation of fact
the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
items.s: Abettor: a person who incites or encourages the doer at the moment the act takes place. The other options describe Intention, Housebreaking, Obtaining by false pretences.

items.q: Rape may be defined as
o: unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement
a killing for which the actor is not blamed, as in a pure accident without fault
a person who assists or encourages beforehand without being present at the act
a killing that would otherwise be the gravest form but for a mitigating factor such as provocation
items.s: Rape: unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without her free agreement. The other options describe Accessory before the fact, Excusable homicide, Voluntary manslaughter.

items.q: Assault may be defined as
o: the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
an act that puts another in fear of immediate unlawful force
the free agreement of a person to what would otherwise be a wrong against him
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
items.s: Assault: an act that puts another in fear of immediate unlawful force. The other options describe Housebreaking, Consent, Kidnapping.

items.q: The statement “the reason that drives a person to act, which differs from the purpose to break the law” describes which of the following?
o: Motive
Mens rea
Recklessness
Negligence
items.s: Motive is the reason that drives a person to act, which differs from the purpose to break the law.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Crime?
o: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent
acting without conscious control, as in a convulsion or during sleepwalking
conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts
the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
items.s: Crime: conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts. The other options describe Regulatory offence, Automatism, Abduction.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Which of the following best describes Regulatory offence?
o: the state of being under the influence of drink or drugs, which may negate a required state of mind
responsibility of one person for the act of another, arising from their relationship
a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent
the rule that a guilty state of mind aimed at one person carries over to the person actually hurt
items.s: Regulatory offence: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent. The other options describe Transferred malice, Vicarious liability, Intoxication.

items.q: Mens rea may be defined as
o: securing property or credit through a dishonest representation of fact
a failure to act where the law imposes a duty to act
the blameworthy state of mind that the prosecution must prove for most offences
the state of being under the influence of drink or drugs, which may negate a required state of mind
items.s: Mens rea: the blameworthy state of mind that the prosecution must prove for most offences. The other options describe Intoxication, Obtaining by false pretences, Omission.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Justifiable homicide.
o: a charge tried by a magistrate without any formal indictment
any offence that the law does not class as a felony and that carries a lighter penalty
a killing that the law permits, as in the execution of a lawful death sentence
the quality of acting without any claim of right and in disregard of the owner's interest
items.s: Justifiable homicide: a killing that the law permits, as in the execution of a lawful death sentence. The other options describe Misdemeanour, Summary offence, Dishonesty.

items.q: The statement “the quality of acting without any claim of right and in disregard of the owner's interest” describes which of the following?
o: Mens rea
Transferred malice
Knowledge
Dishonesty
items.s: Dishonesty is the quality of acting without any claim of right and in disregard of the owner's interest.

items.q: Knowledge may be defined as
o: the person whose own act fulfils the definition of the crime
the blameworthy state of mind that the prosecution must prove for most offences
awareness that a certain fact exists
a killing that would otherwise be the gravest form but for a mitigating factor such as provocation
items.s: Knowledge: awareness that a certain fact exists. The other options describe Principal offender, Mens rea, Voluntary manslaughter.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Causing death by dangerous driving?
o: the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct
an offence committed when a motorist's poor control of a vehicle results in a fatality
a failure to act where the law imposes a duty to act
the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer
items.s: Causing death by dangerous driving: an offence committed when a motorist's poor control of a vehicle results in a fatality. The other options describe Reformation, Deterrence, Omission.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Attempt?
o: a step taken with the purpose of committing a crime that does not reach completion
carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree
the taking away or confinement of a person without lawful authority
a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent
items.s: Attempt: a step taken with the purpose of committing a crime that does not reach completion. The other options describe Kidnapping, Regulatory offence, Defilement.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Infanticide?
o: the killing of a newly born child by its mother while her mind is disturbed by the effect of birth
the reason that drives a person to act, which differs from the purpose to break the law
the actual application of unlawful force to the body of another
the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
items.s: Infanticide: the killing of a newly born child by its mother while her mind is disturbed by the effect of birth. The other options describe Motive, Housebreaking, Battery.

items.q: Which term is described by “a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless”?
o: Mistake of fact
Alibi
Consent
Intoxication
items.s: Mistake of fact is a wrong belief about circumstances which, if true, would make the act blameless.

items.q: Robbery may be defined as
o: the taking of property by force or threat of force at or immediately before the taking
the situation where the intended crime cannot be committed, which may still ground liability for the step taken
a person who helps the wrongdoer to escape detection once the act is complete
a person who incites or encourages the doer at the moment the act takes place
items.s: Robbery: the taking of property by force or threat of force at or immediately before the taking. The other options describe Impossibility, Abettor, Accessory after the fact.

items.q: Which term is described by “responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element”?
o: Vicarious liability
Strict liability
Absolute liability
Due diligence
items.s: Strict liability is responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element.

items.q: The statement “securing property or credit through a dishonest representation of fact” describes which of the following?
o: Obtaining by false pretences
Receiving
Conversion
Armed robbery
items.s: Obtaining by false pretences is securing property or credit through a dishonest representation of fact.

the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct
the dishonest taking of another's property with intent permanently to deprive
the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
items.s: Motive: the reason that drives a person to act, which differs from the purpose to break the law. The other options describe Deterrence, Abduction, Theft.

items.q: The statement “responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element” describes which of the following?
o: Due diligence
Strict liability
Absolute liability
Corporate criminal liability
items.s: Strict liability is responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element.

o: a charge tried by a magistrate without any formal indictment
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
the link that must be shown between the conduct of the accused and the prohibited result
a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial
items.s: Indictable offence: a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial. The other options describe Causation, Beyond reasonable doubt, Summary offence.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Crime.
o: any act or omission for which the law imposes a penalty
a person who advises or instructs another beforehand to carry out the crime
awareness that a certain fact exists
conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts
items.s: Crime: conduct that the state prohibits and punishes through its courts. The other options describe Offence, Knowledge, Counsellor.

items.q: Which term is described by “the state of being under the influence of drink or drugs, which may negate a required state of mind”?
o: Alibi
Intoxication
Automatism
Mistake of fact
items.s: Intoxication is the state of being under the influence of drink or drugs, which may negate a required state of mind.

o: Novus actus interveniens

Causation
items.s: Novus actus interveniens is a new intervening event that breaks the chain between the conduct and the result.

the test asking whether the result would have happened without the conduct of the accused
responsibility that arises even where the accused took every possible care
the prohibited conduct or consequence, with any required circumstances, that makes up the physical side of an offence
items.s: Factual causation: the test asking whether the result would have happened without the conduct of the accused. The other options describe Actus reus, Offence, Absolute liability.

responsibility for a prohibited act without proof of any mental element
a killing that the law permits, as in the execution of a lawful death sentence

the link that must be shown between the conduct of the accused and the prohibited result
items.s: Regulatory offence: a breach of a statute on standards such as food, traffic or safety, punished without proof of intent. The other options describe Indictable offence, Kidnapping, Causation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Abduction?
o: the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end
any offence that the law does not class as a felony and that carries a lighter penalty
carnal knowledge of a child below the stated age, even where the child appeared to agree
items.s: Abduction: the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end. The other options describe Housebreaking, Defilement, Misdemeanour.

items.q: Which term is described by “the taking away of a young person by force or deceit for an unlawful end”?
o: Assault
Abduction
Kidnapping
Defilement

o: the shared design of persons acting together, which makes each liable for what follows in its pursuit
the person whose own act fulfils the definition of the crime
a person who advises or instructs another beforehand to carry out the crime
a person who helps the wrongdoer to escape detection once the act is complete
items.s: Common purpose: the shared design of persons acting together, which makes each liable for what follows in its pursuit. The other options describe Counsellor, Accessory after the fact, Principal offender.

items.q: Receiving may be defined as
o: the act of breaking and entering a building with intent to commit a grave offence in it
dealing with another's property as though one were its owner
taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen
a taking of property by a person carrying a dangerous weapon at the time
items.s: Receiving: taking into possession goods that one knows to have been stolen. The other options describe Conversion, Housebreaking, Armed robbery.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Reformation?
o: the aim of punishment that seeks to frighten others away from similar conduct
the degree of certainty a court must reach before it finds a fact established
the high measure of assurance required in a criminal trial before conviction
the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer
items.s: Reformation: the aim of punishment that seeks to correct and improve the character of the wrongdoer. The other options describe Beyond reasonable doubt, Deterrence, Standard of proof.
items.t: Nature and purpose of criminal law

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Indictable offence.
o: a crime for which the law prescribes the death penalty
a minor infraction tried in a lower court and punished by a small fine or short detention
a charge tried by a magistrate without any formal indictment
a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial
items.s: Indictable offence: a charge that must be tried on information after the accused has been committed for trial. The other options describe Capital offence, Simple offence, Summary offence.

items.q: “a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless” is the definition of
o: Justifiable homicide
Causing death by dangerous driving
Involuntary manslaughter
Manslaughter
items.s: Involuntary manslaughter is a killing without any intent to kill or injure, where the conduct was unlawful or very careless.
